 Oral Judgment
(Per: The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vijaykumar A.Patil)

This appeal is by the claimant/land
loser challenging the judgment & award dated 21.04.2018 passed in Lac No.4/2010 on the file of
learned Iii Addl. Senior Civil Judge, Belagavi1, whereby the market value of the subject land is
determined at the rate of Rs.20,000/- per gunta with all statutory benefits and interest.
2.  Brief facts leading to filing of this appeal are that the appellant filed a claim petition under Section 18(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 18942 seeking compensation.
It is averred that the appellant is the owner of land measuring 39 guntas in RS No.241/1 of Halaga Village, Belagavi Taluk and District.
The land of the appellant was acquired by the State Government vide Preliminary Notification dated 4.12.2008 for the purpose of construction of Suvarna Soudha at Belagavi.

The Special Land Acquisition Officer, Belagavi3, has passed an award on 6.6.2009 awarding a total compensation of Rs.5,26,398/- for the acquired land with all statutory benefits 'Reference Court', for short 'Act,
1894', for short 'SLAO', for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:11239-DB and interest.
It is averred that the acquired land is very near to National Highway-4 and it has non-agricultural potentiality.
It is also averred that the acquired land is just 7 kms away from the centre of Belgaum City and the acquired land is surrounded by Hotels, Dhabas, Garages and Showrooms.

It is pleaded that within 4 kms away from the acquired land, there are educational institutions and other commercial establishments and without considering the same, the SLAO has determined the market value of the subject land on the lower side.
However, the acquired land fetches more than Rs.4,00,000/- per gunta.
3. The respondent entered appearance before the Reference Court and opposed the claim petition.

It is averred that the SLAO has taken into account the relevant factors and determined the market value of the acquired land, which does not call for any enhancement and sought dismissal of the claim petition.
4. Before the Reference Court, the claimant examined himself as PW1 and one Sri. Mallikarjun Mudnur, Approved Valuer examined as PW2 and produced eight documents as Ex.P1 to P8.
The respondent did not adduce any oral evidence, NC: 2024:KHC-D:11239-DB however, with consent Shri.

Sadanand S/O. Vigneshwar Hegade vs The Assistnat Commissioner on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17600211/
2 got marked Ex.R1 and R2.

entities.text: Sadanand S/O. Vigneshwar Hegade vs The Assistnat Commissioner on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Reference Court on appreciation of the pleadings and evidence available on record determined the market value of the acquired land at Rs.20,000/- per gunta and also awarded the statutory benefits and interest.
Being aggrieved, the claimant/land loser is in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.

5. Sri. Jagadish Patil, learned counsel appearing for the appellant reiterating the grounds of appeal submits that the Reference Court has erred in appreciating the evidence available on record and awarded compensation of Rs.20,000/- per gunta, which is on the lower side.

It is submitted that the acquired land is highly potential land for commercial activity and adjacent to National Highway,
hence, he seeks to re-assess the evidence and award higher compensation to the land loser.

It is further submitted that the land in question was acquired in the year 2008 and at that time,
surrounding lands were partially developed and distance from the acquired land to Belgaum City is less than 7 kms and within the distance of 4-5 kms, there are Educational Institutions, Show-rooms,
Hotels, Commercial Establishments etc.
Hence, these factors are also NC: 2024:KHC-D:11239-DB required to be taken note of while determining the market value of the acquired land.
It is also submitted that the NHAI has acquired the portion of the land of the appellant in the year 2001 and awarded total compensation of Rs.20,085/- for 390 sq.mtrs. of land.
He seeks to apply escalation of 10% to the aforesaid amount for a period of 7 years and determine the land in question and seeks to allow the appeal.

6. Per contra, learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondent supports the impugned judgment and award of the Reference Court and submits that the Reference Court taking note of the evidence available on record has awarded just and fair compensation to the appellant, same does not call for any enhancement.
It is submitted that the NHAI's acquisition is only 390 sq.mtrs. of the land and such a small extent cannot be the basis to determine the land in question and hence, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

7. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused material on record including trial Court records meticulously, the only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is as to,
whether the impugned judgment and award of the Reference Court calls for interference in this appeal.

The appellant's land measuring 39 guntas in RS No.241/1 of Halaga village of Belagavi Taluk and District was acquired by the State Government for the purpose of construction of Suvarna Soudha at Belagavi vide Preliminary Notification dated 4.12.2008.
The SLAO passed the award dated 6.6.2009 awarding total compensation of Rs.5,26,398/- for the acquired land.

In order to seek higher compensation, the claimant examined himself as PW1, he has reiterated the averments made in the claim petition by contending that the acquired land is adjacent to National Highway and highly potential for commercial use.

In his evidence, he deposed that the adjacent lands have partially developed and the distance between the acquired land and Belgaum city is 7 kms and within distance of 4-5 kms, there are Educational Institutions, Commercial Establishments, Show-rooms and Hotels etc.

In his evidence, he got marked reference petition as Ex.P1, RTC extract as Ex.P2 and Shri.Sadanand S/O. Vigneshwar Hegade vs The Assistnat Commissioner on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17600211/
3 certified copy of the consent award as Ex.P3.
Ex . P3 indicates that State has acquired 105 acres 19 guntas and 11 annas, out of that, 99 acres 31 guntas, a consent award is passed, wherein land value is shown as Rs.13,46,96,221/-.
Ex.P4 is the statement enclosed to award NC: 2024:KHC-D:11239-DB at Ex.P3, which indicates that SLAO has fixed the market value at Rs.13,50,000/- per acre.

9. The SLAO has determined the market value of the acquired land of the appellant at Rs.3,88,420/-
per acre as per Ex.R1.

It is also not in dispute that insofar as remaining extent of acquired land under the same notification, a consent award is passed by the SLAO by determining the market value at Rs.13,50,000/- per acre, i.e. Rs.33,750/- per gunta.
This consent award does not include any statutory benefits and interest.
Hence, award of Reference Court at Rs.20,000/- per Gunta is on lower side, required to be interfered in the present appeal.
The appellant herein has not consented to the passing of the consent award, hence, separate award is passed by the SLAO at Ex.R1.
Thereafter, the Reference Court enhanced the same to Rs.20,000/- per gunta with statutory benefits and interest, based on the evidence on record.
10. The appellant in order to claim higher compensation examined the Government Approved Valuer as PW2 and his Valuation Report is produced and marked as Ex.P5.

The Report of PW2 indicates that the acquired land is situated in Halaga village, and the distance from Belgaum bus stand is 7.75 kms NC: 2024:KHC-D:11239-DB from the acquired land and surrounding lands are developed.

The Report of the Expert at Ex.P5 indicates that the Approved Valuer has produced copies of guideline rates issued by the Department of Stamps and Registration, Government of Karnataka for the respective year.

entities.text: Department of Stamps and Registration, Government of Karnataka
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The guidelines value for the year 2007-08 for commercial site in Halaga Village is Rs.40 per sq.ft. and for the year 2009-10, Rs.48 per sq.ft. is fixed.
The guidelines value referred supra is on sq.ft. basis and it is for the commercial site.
Hence, the said Guideline Value cannot be applied as it is to the land in question, admittedly, the land in question being agricultural land.

The Expert in his Report at Ex.P5 under clause No.4.3.2, is of the opinion that the acquired land is adjacent to National Highway and highly potential and commands a minimum 50%
higher value when compared to lands situated on interior roads.

Based on such appreciation, he has calculated the market value of the acquired land at Rs.44 per sq.ft. and added 50% to the said rate and comes to a conclusion that the market value would be Rs.66 per sq.ft. or Rs.71,874/- per gunta.

In our considered view, the approach of the Expert Valuer cannot be fully relied upon to determine the market value of the land in question for the reason that the NC: 2024:KHC-D:11239-DB acquired land though it is adjacent to National Highway and potential for commercial use, the land in question is admittedly an agricultural land.

Hence, we are not in agreement with the Approved Valuer's assessment of the market value at Rs.66 per sq.ft.
11.

Another aspect we have kept in mind is that the consent award passed by the SLAO indicates that the market value of the acquired land is Rs.13,50,000/- i.e., Rs.33,750/- per gunta without any statutory benefits and the NHAI, which acquired the portion of the land, awarded Rs.20,085/- for 390 sq.mtrs. of the land, however, the said land was acquired in the year 2001.

In the instant case,
the acquisition is of the year 2008.

Hence, the award of compensation by the NHAI at Ex.P8 would not help the appellant anyway nor the consent Award should be basis to decide the market value &
the land in question.
Admittedly, the appellant has not placed any other legally acceptable evidence on record to establish the market value of the acquired land in question.
Ex. P6
and Ex

. P7 are the Shri.Sadanand S/O. Vigneshwar Hegade vs The Assistnat Commissioner on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17600211/
4 judgments passed in LAC Nos.40 to 43 of 2007 and certified copy of the award.

entities.text: Shri.Sadanand S/O. Vigneshwar Hegade vs The Assistnat Commissioner
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The lands involved in the said judgments are away from the land in question and it cannot be a basis to - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11239-DB come to a correct conclusion with regard to market value of the acquired land.

12. On considering the oral and documentary evidence on record and taking note of the observation in Ex.P5-Valuation Report and oral testimony of PW2, we are of the view that that it would be just and appropriate to consider the market value of the subject land at the rate of Rs.30 per sq.ft.

Keeping in mind the fact that the land in question is admittedly an agricultural land, though the land is having potential for commercial activity, cannot assess the market value of the land as commercial property on square foot basis.

We have appropriately deducted the cost of development and applied the same to the guideline value of State Government enclosed with the Valuation Report i.e., the guidelines value issued by the State Government for the year 2007-08 is Rs.40 per sq.ft. for the commercial site at Halaga village and keeping the said factor in mind, we assess the market value of the agricultural land at Rs.30 per sq.ft., in other words, Rs.32,670/- per gunta (Rs.30 x 1089 sq.ft.), which would meet the ends of justice.

13. The Reference Court has not assigned any reason whatsoever in determining the market value of the acquired - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11239-DB land at Rs.20,000/- per gunta and such finding of the Reference Court is without any basis and contrary to the evidence available on record, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court and accordingly, we re
-assess the market value of the acquired land at Rs.32,670/- per gunta.

14. This Court keeping in mind the settled principles of law and also keeping in mind the fact that the land is near the Belgaum City and having potential for commercial activity, we are of the considered view that interest of justice would be met if we re-determine the market value of the subject land at Rs.30 sq.ft. or Rs.32,670/- per gunta as against Rs.20,000/- per gunta determined by the Reference Court.

15. For the foregoing reasons, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal filed by the claimant is partly allowed with costs.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Reference Court is modified by re-determining the market value of the subject land at Shri.Sadanand S/O. Vigneshwar Hegade vs The Assistnat Commissioner on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17600211/
5 - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11239-DB Rs.32,670/- (Thirty Two Thousand Six Seventy Rupees Only) per gunta with solatium, statutory benefits and interest as per the provision of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

d) Registry shall transmit back the original TCR to the Reference Court forthwith.
e) Registry to draw modified award accordingly.
